body.en: We fix an origin and a positive direction on a line. *Position* x is measured from the origin. Displacement is the change in position, $\Delta x = x_2 - x_1$, and has a sign. Path length is the total distance travelled and is never negative.

title.en: Displacement, path length and average velocity

say.en: Fix an origin O and a positive direction. Position is read from the origin, in metres.
A girl walks from A at 1 m to B at 6 m, then back to C at 3 m. Displacement is final minus initial position; path length adds every metre walked.
If the walk took 4 seconds, average velocity uses displacement but average speed uses path length.
On a position–time graph, the average velocity is the slope of the chord joining the two instants.

narration.en: The car drives out to x = +30 m, turns round at t = 6 s and comes back past the start. Pick two times. Displacement is the change in position; distance is the length of road actually covered. Average velocity = displacement ÷ time, the slope of the chord on the x–t graph; average speed = distance ÷ time.

problem.en: A car goes 6 km east in 10 min and then 2 km west in 5 min. Find its average velocity and average speed.

steps.en: Displacement = 6 − 2 = 4 km east; path length = 6 + 2 = 8 km.
Average velocity = 4 / 0.25 = 16 km/h east; average speed = 8 / 0.25 = 32 km/h.

narration.en: Let us solve this together. A car goes 6 km east in 10 min and then 2 km west in 5 min. Find its average velocity and average speed.

say.en: Let us solve this together. A car goes 6 kilometres east in 10 minutes and then 2 kilometres west in 5 minutes. Find its average velocity and average speed.
Displacement equals 6 minus 2 equals 4 kilometres east; path length equals 6 plus 2 equals 8 kilometres.
Time equals 15 minutes equals 0.25 hours.
Average velocity equals 4 divided by 0.25 equals 16 kilometres per hour east; average speed equals 8 divided by 0.25 equals 32 kilometres per hour.
So the answer is 16 kilometres per hour east; 32 kilometres per hour.

heading.en: Equal distances? Use the harmonic mean

body.en: For two equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is 2v₁v₂/(v₁ + v₂) — never the simple average.

narration.en: Equal distances? Use the harmonic mean. For two equal distances at speeds v₁ and v₂, the average speed is 2v₁v₂/(v₁ + v₂) — never the simple average.

mnemonic.en: Equal Distance → Double Product over Sum

say.en: Equal distances? Use the harmonic mean. For two equal distances at speeds v 1 and v 2, the average speed is 2v 1v 2 over v 1 plus v 2, never the simple average.
